VERTEX EDITOR · QUICK GUIDE

Anchor: resize around one vertex

Anchor holds one vertex still while the others resize around it.

1. Select and set Anchor

Select three vertices (Shift-click to add). Press Z, then hold 1 while dragging a box around the vertex to keep fixed.

2. Resize

Drag in empty viewport space. The green Anchor stays in place.

VERTEX EDITOR · QUICK GUIDE

Align: line up three spike tips

All three bases overlap in Front view. Only the forward and rear tips lean left and right. Align them to the straight middle tip, then rotate to see three equal, upright spikes.

1. Select the tips and set Align

In Front view, select the three tips. Press Z, then Shift+1. Drag a box around the middle tip.

2. Align from the front

Pull until Front view shows one complete spike.

3. Inspect from another view

Rotate upward and sideways. The three separate spikes are the same size and point the same way; their tips lined up according to the Front viewpoint.

UV WRAPPER · QUICK GUIDE

Live Select: manipulate UV coordinates live

Live Select lets you select one or more vertices in the live 3D preview while working in the UV map, then manipulate their UV coordinates immediately. Use it to separate overlapping coordinates.

1. Select vertices in the live preview

Hold A and drag over visible vertices in the live preview. Their matching UV coordinates become selected.

2. Separate overlapping coordinates

Select another visible set with A + click. Press Ctrl+E to include connected vertices, then M for Move. Drag its UV coordinates away from the overlap. Repeat for other visible sets.

AUTO CORPSE · QUICK GUIDE

Auto Corpse: adjust the fit

Use the body as a reference, then adjust any parts that need a closer fit.

1. Compare the fit

Keep Body outline on. Toggle Show body to compare the generated corpse with the body, then turn it off to see the parts clearly.

2. Move, stretch and widen parts

Double-click a part. Drag the center handle to move it, an end handle to stretch it, and the side handle to adjust its width. Use the outline to judge the fit; repeat wherever needed.

3. Set height and tint

Use Height to lower or raise the bones; this example uses 80%. Set Color Tint to R 225 · G 255 · B 100 for the result shown. Check Show body again, then click Create when the fit is right. Auto Corpse also sets up Decay Flesh and Decay Bone, including body and corpse visibility.

Glow Up: add hero glow

Add hero glow, adjust its ground size, and inspect the result.

1. Open Glow Up

From the main screen, click EMTR, then Glow Up.

2. Adjust the ground glow

Pause the preview. Drag the ground-glow edge a little to adjust its size.

3. Create and inspect

Click Create and close EMTR. Open Animations, select Stand and press Play. Alt-drag to inspect the glows during playback.

EMTR: ribbons during a swing

Add a fitted ribbon and control the visible part of an attack.

1. Create the fitted ribbon

With the weapon faces already marked, open EMTR and choose Add ribbon. Under Visibility, check only the attack animation you want, then choose Create. Leave other animations unchecked.

2. Set the blue diamonds and trail lifetime

Keep the ribbon off for the first 20% of the attack. Put the first blue diamond at 20% and the second at 100%. Use a longer Lasts value for a clearly visible sweep across the remaining 80%.

3. Watch the complete animation

Play the complete attack and inspect another angle. The first fifth should have no ribbon; the remaining four fifths should show the full sweep. Check an unchecked animation too.

Longer sweep
Lasts controls how long existing trail pieces remain. A longer value makes the sweep longer.

Time each animation separately
Repeat the timing for each animation that should show the ribbon. The animation checkboxes choose where it is enabled; the blue diamonds set the interval within the selected animation. Unchecked animations stay hidden.

OptimizeXL: review every change

Clean up data and reduce file size while checking that the model still looks and moves as intended. Keep only changes you have inspected.

Open the green-marked OPXL button, or press O.

1. Compare the original and the proposal

Before stays fixed to the original. After shows approved changes plus the current proposal. Choose an Animation, play with Space, then rotate and zoom: both views follow together.

2. Reduce carefully

Review structural repairs first. In Duplicate data and Animation optimization, start at low Strength and increase gradually. Open Geosets to review or Changed animations and inspect the affected details before Approve.

Insanity FIxer

Checks structure and proposes supported repairs. Select a finding or preview a group; some require a Choice or manual editing.

Inspect the affected animation or effect. Fix everything previews a batch using default choices; it still needs approval. A clean report does not prove that every animation looks right.

Duplicate data

Merges compatible duplicated vertex data, bone groups and equivalent leaf bones, and removes suitable repeated triangles. It does not merge separate geosets together.

Zoom in on small openings, overlapping surfaces, hard edges and texture details. More strength allows larger differences.

Animation optimization

Removes redundant animation keys. Higher strength allows larger differences. Local tracks is the default; World-space bound compares the posed mesh within a tolerance.

Watch all relevant animations: subtle motion, weapon tips, joints, loops and death/decay transitions. Lower strength if the intended movement changes.

3. Inspect motion, visibility and bounds

Play and scrub the affected animations slowly. Check subtle movements, textures and effects, including the moments around a proposed repair. Use Skip fix for intentional motion. In Sphereomancer, inspect the collision spheres from several angles.

Unused data

Removes vertices unused by triangles, unreferenced resources and unused rig nodes. Geometry hidden in one animation is not automatically unused.

Read Data to remove. Check materials, textures and effects afterwards; remaining checker notices may need separate review.

Irregularities Fixer

Suggests repairs for suspicious visibility, pose mismatches, jitter, sudden movement and distortion. Selecting a finding opens its animation and frame.

Unusual motion may be intentional. Orange/red flags indicate review priority, not certainty. Inspect only findings have no automatic fix. Skip a repair that spoils intended motion.

Sphereomancer

Adjusts collision spheres used to click/select the model. Choose a preset and Size, or edit each sphere in Advanced.

Inspect coverage from several angles. Size changes selection bounds, not visible geometry. Approval replaces current collision shapes.

Nuclear Polygon Destroyer

A ridiculous tool for fun. Reduces triangles until the result can become a deliberately mangled experiment.

Try it separately and Skip stage to leave it out of normal cleanup. Watch the silhouette, holes, textures and moving joints. Protection may prevent reaching the target count.

4. Keep only the result you want

Approve keeps a proposal inside OptimizeXL. Back undoes the last approval or skipped stage. Commit returns approved changes to the editor without saving; Save writes them to the file. Unapproved previews are never included.

Look closely before approving

Shape and texture
Zoom in and rotate. Check openings, thin parts, hard edges, texture seams and overlapping layers.

Motion and visibility
Watch full loops and transitions at normal and slow speed. Look for lost subtle motion, new snaps, floating parts, changed effects or objects appearing at the wrong time.

Size is not the verdict
Keep a larger result if it preserves the intended look and motion. Lower strength, skip a proposal or use Back when a change makes the model worse.

Final check
Review all relevant animations before saving. A clean report or a good editor preview does not by itself verify the model in Warcraft III.

Controls and Advanced settings

Reading and approving
Before · After
Before remains the original; After includes approved work and the current proposal. Camera and playback controls affect both panes.
Simple · Advanced · Strength
Simple offers strength; Advanced exposes tolerances. Zero still performs exact duplicate/key cleanup, but no Nuclear reduction. Hover a setting or click its i for help.
Approve · Skip stage · Next stage · Back
Approve keeps the proposal; Skip stage leaves it out. Next stage leaves a repair stage. Back undoes the last approval or skipped stage. Changing stage discards an unapproved preview.
Geosets to review · Changed animations · Data to remove
Inspect the affected parts, animations or records. A green stage star means there are changes to review, not that they should be accepted.
Animation · Play · Pause · Start · End · Speed (%) · Loop
Space plays/pauses; the frame slider scrubs. Start/End jump to the endpoints. Speed: 100 normal, 0 held pose, 200 double speed. Loop repeats.
Exclude geosets · Highlight Geoset · All · Clear · Invert
Checked parts stay visible but are excluded from reductions. All/Clear/Invert alter the set. Hover highlights the part. Exclusions do not apply to repairs or spheres.
Reviewing findings
Proposed fixes · Findings · Choice
Selecting a finding opens its animation and frame. Read any Choice alternatives before approving. Some findings are inspection only.
Fix everything · Approve all fixes
Previews supported batch repairs with default choices and checks again. Review before approving; some risky or manual cases remain separate.
Select fixes · Select all · Clear all · Preview all selected fixes · Approve selected
Choose checkboxes, preview together, then approve. Changing the selection clears the old preview until the new selection is previewed.
Skip fix · Skip selected · Cancel
Leave a finding or selected group unchanged. Cancel exits the Fix everything preview without approving it.
Static gravity · Use the destination pose as the reference instead
Shown only for relevant repairs. Static gravity can change particles; reversing the pose reference changes which endpoint is copied. Inspect the result.
Duplicate data — Advanced
Position tolerance
Allowed position difference for merging; higher values can affect small details. Zero requires identical positions.
UV tolerance · Normal angle (degrees)
UV tolerance controls texture-coordinate differences; Normal angle controls surface directions. Higher values may shift textures or soften edges.
Merge equivalent leaf bones
Combines identical bones without children while retaining their movement.
Animation optimization — Advanced
Reduction method · Local tracks · World-space bound
Local tracks is the default. World-space bound compares posed-mesh differences. Both still require visual review.
Translation tolerance · Rotation tolerance (degrees) · Scale tolerance
Allowed movement, rotation and scale differences. Raise only as needed; inspect subtle motion and long-part endpoints.
World-space tolerance
Allowed sampled mesh difference in model units. Slow animations use tighter limits. It does not guarantee identical motion at every instant.
Unused data — Advanced
Unreferenced vertices
Removes vertices unused by triangles and bone groups unused by remaining vertices.
Unused materials, textures and globals
Removes unused resources and merges identical texture records. Resources referenced by animations or effects remain.
Unused bones and helpers · Review mdx-m3-viewer cleanup
Removes unused rig nodes while keeping needed ancestors. Review remaining checker notices separately through the cleanup button.
Sphereomancer — controls
Preset · Small unit · Standard unit · Large unit · Tall unit · Mounted rider
Choose a starting arrangement, then check the fit. Presets are starting points, not automatic detection.
Size · X · Y · Z · Radius
Size scales group positions and radii together. Advanced edits each center and radius; Z controls height.
Add sphere
Adds a sphere to the proposal. The × beside a sphere removes it. Keep changes only after reviewing and approving.
Nuclear Polygon Destroyer — Advanced
Target polygons · Shape/texture error (%)
Target polygons is the count to aim for. A higher error budget allows more shape/texture damage; it is not a percentage of pixels changed.
Sharp-edge angle · Protect sharp edges
The angle determines which hard edges are protected. Keeping protection can limit reduction.
Protect UV seams and boundaries · Protect skinning boundaries
Preserve UV seams, open borders and bone-binding boundaries. Disabling them allows more destruction; inspect textures and moving joints.
Keep the approved result
Commit
Applies approved work to the open model as one undoable edit and returns to the editor. It does not save the file.
Save · Back up, then save · Save without backup
Save writes approved work to the current model file. When offered, the backup option copies the existing disk file first; saving without backup writes directly.
Close · Close without saving · Cancel
With unsaved approved work, Close offers Save, Commit, Close without saving or Cancel. Commit and Save never include unapproved previews.

FX · QUICK GUIDE

FX: introduction

Apply a preset to one surface, add an emitter, adjust the look, and check it in motion.

1. Choose a surface effect

Open FX. Choose the target geoset, then choose an effect from the library.

2. Add and adjust

Use Add emitter to add particles. Select a layer and adjust its Intensity in the live preview.

3. Review and apply

Rotate the preview to inspect the result. Click Apply effect to commit it to the model.

4. Check animations

In Animations, play Attack and then Walk to check the effect as the surface moves.

Advanced functions

Available controls depend on the selected preset and layer.

Target and preview
Geoset
Chooses the whole surface that receives the effect.
Highlight geoset · Solo · Fit selection
Highlight identifies the target; Solo hides other parts in the preview; Fit selection frames the target.
Original
Temporarily shows the model without the current FX preview. It does not discard the draft.
Overlay and layers
Create as overlay
Keeps the original surface visible and draws the effect on a separate surface above it. With it off, a surface preset can replace the original appearance.
Layers
Click a layer to edit its controls. Its checkbox enables or disables that layer.
Add layer · Remove layer
Combines extra surface, glow, rune or edge layers, or removes the selected layer.
Timing, colour and glow
Loop length
Duration of one FX cycle in milliseconds. It does not change the model animation length.
Colour · Reset
Tints the selected layer; Reset restores that layer’s default colour.
Intensity · Glow
Intensity changes the selected layer’s strength. Glow layers can exceed 100%. Glow selects their pulse or flicker pattern.
Texture and movement
Change texture
Chooses the selected layer’s image from the game texture library.
Speed · Direction · Tiling
Adjusts texture passes per FX loop, travel direction, and repetition across the surface.
Move UVs · Rotate UVs · Scale UVs
Changes the texture placement on the selected layer. The model geometry stays in place.
Emitters
Add emitter · Change emitter
Adds particles to the stack or swaps the selected emitter. The recommended choice belongs to the current preset.
Amount · Lasts · Size
Controls emission rate, how long particles remain visible, and their visible size.
Speed · Rise / Fall
Controls initial particle motion and acceleration as particles age.
Born · Halfway · End
Sets particle colour, size and transparency over their lifetime.
Position & size
Shows handles for moving and fitting the selected emitter in the preview.
Open in EMTR
Applies the current FX stack, then opens the selected emitter in the full emitter editor.
Keep or discard
Apply effect
Commits the shown geoset’s FX as one undoable edit. It does not save the model file to disk.
Cancel
Closes FX without applying its uncommitted changes.

UV WRAPPER · QUICK GUIDE

UV grid and snapping

Align the Slaanesh Knight’s horse-cloth pattern. Start with the cloth geometry selected in UV Wrapper.

1. Set the grid

Turn on Grid. Adjust Size, or enter an exact value in Settings → Spacing. Turn on Snap.

2. Snap one vertex

Choose Move and drag one selected UV vertex. It automatically snaps to grid crossings as you drag.

3. Move a group by grid cells

Keep Grid and Snap on. Use the numeric keypad to move selected UV vertices together: one current grid cell per press on each active axis. Diagonals move one cell on both axes. Press 6 three times to move three cells right; the group keeps its relative spacing.

Numeric keypad

7 ↖8 ↑9 ↗4 ←56 →1 ↙2 ↓3 ↘

Num Lock can be on or off. Click the UV map before using the keypad.

Vertex editor

Spread pieces

Move the two weapons of the Warrior of Slaanesh · Slayer closer or farther apart at full size. Start with both weapons selected in Vertices.

1. Shrink with Resize

Press Z for Resize and drag left. Both weapons shrink into a single point. Press Ctrl + Z to undo.

2. Bring them together at full size

Start another Resize drag and hold Ctrl. Drag left until the weapons meet at the pivot, then drag right to spread them back apart. Keep Ctrl held until you release the mouse.

Spread pieces follows connected geometry. For these clips, the weapon meshes were joined into one piece per weapon in a recording copy of the model.
